title: Chronic and subacute phenylalanine effects on brain metabolism in adults with phenylketonuria
title_zh: 苯丙氨酸对苯丙酮酸症成人脑代谢的慢性和亚急性影响
abstract: Abstract Phenylketonuria (PKU) leads to chronic cerebral exposure to elevated phenylalanine (Phe) despite lifelong dietary treatment, yet the neurometabolic consequences in adulthood remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether adults with early-treated PKU exhibit persistent alterations in brain metabolism and whether these metabolites respond dynamically to subacute Phe fluctuations. Adults with early-treated PKU (n=30) and healthy controls (n=59) underwent proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS), structural and functional brain MRI to evaluate white matter lesion load (T2-weighted images) and cerebral blood flow (arterial spin labeling), as well as cognitive assessments. Patients additionally participated in a randomized, placebo-controlled crossover intervention with four weeks of oral Phe loading to evaluate subacute metabolic responsiveness. Absolute metabolite concentrations were quantified in predominantly white matter tissue, and associations between blood and brain Phe, white matter lesion load, cerebral blood flow, and cognitive performance were examined. At baseline, patients exhibited higher brain Phe and N-acetylaspartate (NAA) levels, alongside reduced myo-inositol, N-acetylaspartylglutamate (NAAG), and total creatine/phosphocreatine compared with controls. Patients with white matter lesions did not differ in blood and brain metabolites from those without. Four weeks of oral Phe loading increased brain Phe and produced a reversible decrease in myo-inositol, whereas NAA, NAAG, and creatine compounds remained unchanged. Blood and brain Phe concentrations were strongly correlated (r=0.83, p<0.001), and their ratio was subject-dependent. No significant associations were observed between metabolite concentrations and regional cerebral blood flow or cognitive performance after correction for multiple comparisons. Adults with early-treated PKU exhibit persistent neurometabolic alterations involving neuronal–glial metabolism, energy buffering, and astrocytic osmolyte regulation. The findings support a trait–state framework, with stable alterations in NAA, NAAG, and creatine compounds reflecting long-standing metabolic changes, superimposed on a dynamically Phe-sensitive astrocytic response indexed by myo-inositol. The absence of strong associations with cerebral perfusion or cognition suggests that these alterations represent upstream biological processes not captured by macroscopic imaging or behavioral measures.
abstract_zh: 摘要 苯丙酮酸症（PKU）会导致大脑长期暴露于升高的苯丙氨酸（Phe），尽管接受终生饮食治疗，但成年期的神经代谢后果尚未完全阐明。我们研究了早期治疗的 PKU 成人是否持续存在脑代谢改变，以及这些代谢物是否对亚急性 Phe 波动产生动态响应。早期治疗的 PKU 成人（n=30）和健康对照（n=59）接受了质子磁共振波谱（1H-MRS）、结构性和功能性脑 MRI 以评估白质病灶负荷（T2 加权图像）和脑血流（动脉自旋标记），以及认知评估。患者还参加了一项随机、安慰剂对照的交叉干预，进行为期四周的口服 Phe 负荷，以评估亚急性代谢反应性。绝对代谢物浓度主要在白质组织中定量，并检查了血 Phe 和脑 Phe、白质病灶负荷、脑血流与认知表现之间的关联。基线时，患者表现出更高的脑 Phe 和 N-乙酰天冬氨酸（NAA）水平，同时相较于对照组，肌肽酸、N-乙酰天冬氨酰谷氨酸（NAAG）和总肌酸/磷酸肌酸减少。伴有白质病变的患者在血液和脑代谢物上与无病变患者无差异。四周口服 Phe 负荷增加了脑 Phe，并导致肌肽酸可逆性下降，而 NAA、NAAG 和肌酸化合物保持不变。血液和脑 Phe 浓度呈强相关（r=0.83, p<0.001），且其比率呈受试者依赖性。多重比较校正后，未观察到代谢物浓度与区域脑血流或认知表现之间存在显著关联。早期治疗的 PKU 成人表现出涉及神经元-胶质代谢、能量缓冲和星形胶质细胞渗透调节的持续性神经代谢改变。研究结果支持特质-状态框架，NAA、NAAG 和肌酸化合物的稳定改变反映长期存在的代谢改变，叠加以肌肽酸为指标的动态 Phe 敏感星形胶质细胞反应。与脑灌注或认知缺乏强关联表明，这些改变代表宏观影像学或行为指标未捕捉的上游生物学过程。
